what: BF16-ATTN and ATTN-SOFT (2026-10-19): the attention's six products on bfloat16 operands -- bf16+exp+reduce+attnbf16 against the fused binary32 attention, bf16+exp+reduce+attn -- one layer alone and in the 9.84M decoder's step; ATTN-SOFT (the softmax's row maxima over the raw scores, the scale folded into the exponential's argument, every binary32 value as it was) and the AMX kernel split into begin, blocks and end, each timed against the parent commit's library; the A/A controls those library-against-library ratios are read against; one state across the bf16 attention's instances; and the C harness's run without the x86 instances against its caps (the aarch64 CI job's build).
host: Intel(R) Xeon(R) Processor @ 2.10GHz container, 4 vCPUs (AMX-BF16, AVX512-BF16), GCC 13.3 and clang 18.1 (aarch64-timing.txt), Python 3.11.15; head 9a702a4 with this commit's runtime/c in the working tree (df21dda56e866915 against 9a702a4, every record's host line), the base 9a702a4's runtime/c (git archive); the libraries built as the comparison harness builds the trainer (gcc -std=c11 -O3 -ffp-contract=off -fno-math-errno -DBCIR_DT_BUILD_SHARED -shared -fPIC -pthread); indicative wall times, no PMU.
reading: The bf16 attention's layer is faster than the fused binary32 one's in every round at both thread counts (attention-*.txt, one program, the two contracts alternated round by round): one layer's forward x1.163 (95% interval 1.133-1.190, 56 of 61 rounds), backward x1.378 (1.358-1.394, 61 of 61) and the two x1.280 (1.245-1.299, 61 of 61) at four threads; x1.140 (1.127-1.168), x1.327 (1.296-1.356) and x1.230 (1.197-1.243, 31 of 31) at one. The backward gains more: four of the six products are its.

In the 9.84M decoder's step it is a few percent, as the attention's share says: the six layers' attention, timed alone, saves 2.5 ms at four threads (attention-t4.txt), 3.1% of the 80.5 ms step. soft/attnbf16 -- two contracts on one library, no placement between them -- reads x1.029 (1.018-1.042, 96 of 150 rounds) at four threads (steppair-t4.txt) and x1.013 (0.997-1.033) in controls-steppair-t4.txt's run, x1.004 (0.989-1.024) at one thread (steppair-t1.txt).

ATTN-SOFT changes no bit -- soft-*.txt hold the two libraries' forward and backward outputs equal every round, steppair-*.txt the two arms' losses, and identity-attn.json's state under bf16+exp+reduce+attn is 08da09e8..., the ATTN-FMA and BF16-PANELS records' -- and costs nothing a library-against-library ratio on this host resolves: its attention alone reads x1.018 (1.008-1.036) at four threads and x1.017 (1.004-1.027) at one (soft-*.txt, base over this tree, above 1 this tree faster), the step's base/soft x0.990 (0.976-0.998) at four threads and x1.006 (0.982-1.050) at one (steppair-*.txt).

Those are two libraries in one process, and the controls measure what their placement alone does. One source built twice reads base/soft x0.991 (0.977-1.010) in the step pair at four threads (controls-steppair-t4.txt). At one thread the bf16 GEMM reads the parent's library over this tree's at x0.986 (0.976-0.994; gemm-t1.txt), x0.986 with the slots swapped and x0.987 repeated (controls-gemm.txt; every ratio here read as the parent's time over this tree's), and two copies of one library x0.981 (0.974-0.989) and x0.974 (0.960-0.982); at four threads the pair x1.013 (gemm-t4.txt) and the copies x0.991 and x1.008. A process's placement of two libraries moves such a ratio by up to about 3%, and one process's bootstrap interval, which resamples its rounds, cannot see it. Over eight processes, the slots swapped every other one (controls-procs.txt), the parent's GEMM over this tree's is x0.997 (0.993-1.001) at one thread and x1.002 (0.995-1.008) at four, beside the A/A's x0.996 (0.991-1.000) and x1.004 (0.998-1.010): splitting the AMX kernel costs a GEMM nothing measurable, and the step pair's base/soft at four threads is the A/A's own x0.991.

identity-attnbf16.json: one state, fcd6b43b..., under bf16+exp+reduce+attnbf16 through the widest build (AMX), the AVX-512, AVX2 and portable builds at one and four threads and a repeat, six steps of the comparison's decoder; below AVX-512 the bf16 GEMM and attention run as the portable loops, the reference, about 80 s a step at one thread.

aarch64-timing.txt: the C harness built with no x86 dispatch, as the aarch64 CI job builds it -- every bf16 GEMM and attention as the portable loops, the bf16 attention's 304 reference cases on the one instance such a build admits -- passes 27 of 27 in 25.7 s (clang 18) and 27.9 s (GCC 13) of the test's 60 s cap, and under UBSan in 33.2 s and 44.9 s of 300 s, no runtime error. The caps stay; the CI job measures its own host.

files.run.sh: the records in order (bash run.sh TMP DATA [STAGE...] from the repository root): attention, steppair, identity, soft, gemm, controls
files.attention.c: one layer's attention (8 x 128 tokens, 8 query heads over 4 KV heads of 48 channels) alone, forward and backward, under the fused binary32 contract and the bf16 one with the BCIR exponential, on one pool, alternated round by round; ratios fused over bf16
files.steppair.py: the 9.84M decoder's step, three arms in one process a step each in turn, the order rotated: the base under bf16+exp+reduce+attn, this tree under the same and under bf16+exp+reduce+attnbf16; the first two arms' losses asserted equal every round
files.identity-attnbf16.json: the comparison harness's identity stage, six steps under bf16+exp+reduce+attnbf16 through the widest, avx512, avx2 and portable builds at one and four threads, and a repeat: one state
files.identity-attn.json: the same under bf16+exp+reduce+attn (widest): the state of the BF16-PANELS and ATTN-FMA records
files.soft.c: the fused binary32 attention alone, the base's library against this tree's (dlopen, RTLD_LOCAL, each with its own pool), every output compared bit for bit every round
files.gemm.c: the bf16 GEMM alone over five of the decoder's shapes (the gate/up and QKV projections, the down and output projections, a weight adjoint), the same two libraries, C compared bit for bit every round
files.controls-gemm.txt: gemm over two copies of one library (A/A) at one and four threads, the parent's and this tree's with the slots swapped, and gemm-t1's pair repeated
files.procs.py: a gemm pair over several processes, the slots swapped every other one: the processes' ratios, their mean and a 95% Student-t interval
files.controls-procs.txt: procs.py over eight processes: the parent's GEMM over this tree's and the A/A, at one and four threads
files.controls-steppair-t4.txt: steppair.py with this tree as its own base, so its base/soft is an A/A, four threads 150 rounds
files.aarch64-timing.sh, aarch64-timing.txt: the C harness built with BCIR_TENSOR_NO_DISPATCH as the harness test builds it (probes, -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror; and UBSan), under clang and GCC, timed against the test's caps
files.lm/: LM-MULTI: the 1,000-step run, five paired seeds, four arms -- BCIR with the bf16 attention a hundred steps a call, the binary32 attention a hundred steps a call and one, compiled PyTorch bf16 -- run.sh, paired_multi.py (the analysis fixed before the runs), summary.json, the twenty records and lm/README.json: the bf16 attention's test cross-entropy +0.00006 nats from PyTorch bf16's (95% interval -0.00157 to +0.00169), inside the +-0.01 margin, at 2.315 times its tokens a second (2.194-2.444)
